- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.06) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If model consistently underestimates prices during high sentiment (especially >0.20), increase forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, assume momentum bias and adjust next forecast downward by 1–3%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (≥ 3 days), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- When model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, apply lag correction: subtract 1–2% from next forecast to account for delayed price response.
- If sentiment is negative and model forecast is rising, assume sentiment is “reversing” — reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid false bullish momentum.
